reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents CNBC news reporting and an interview about Warren Buffett's stated support for Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan, including discussion of Sloan's departure and Buffett's position. The visible CNBC subscription prompt is ordinary audience engagement and is not explicitly linked to any financial offer or required transaction.

citations.quote: Warren Buffett stands by comments that he supports outgoing Wells Fargo CEO
The two discuss whether Buffett supported Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan, hours before news broke about his retirement.
He said he stands by his comments from yesterday that Tim Sloan does have his full support and also that he doesn't want his job.

opening.argument: Judge, the viewer-facing action and benefit appear together: the description asks viewers to subscribe and offers “exclusive video and more.” That gives viewers a reason to take an action beyond watching the report. The news interview supplies the attraction, while the description directs viewers toward continued access. The evidence does not establish that subscribing is required to see this particular interview, but the subscription invitation should still be weighed as a solicitation tied to an access benefit.

Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately identifies an interview and news report, but that does not account for the separate viewer action in the description. Nor does the absence of a financial offer settle whether the promised access to exclusive material is being used to drive that action. The defense calls the prompt ordinary engagement; the judge should also consider the benefit presented alongside it.

citations.quote: » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those quotes establish a channel subscription prompt and a description of CNBC programming, not an unusually easy reward or a claim that subscribing unlocks this video. The substantive material reports what Buffett said about Sloan and his departure. No supplied evidence links a viewer action to a cash payment, asset, withdrawal, or comparable promised gain.

Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.
He said he stands by his comments from yesterday that Tim Sloan does have his full support and also that he doesn't want his job.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combination of timing and prompts. The report says the interview occurred just hours before the news broke, and the description offers both a subscription link and a link for the latest news. That timing makes the update especially salient; the links give an interested viewer an immediate next step. Neither link establishes a payment or deceptive outcome, but the case for scrutiny is stronger when a time-sensitive financial story and direct calls to click are considered together.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the interview's subject and says the subscription prompt is ordinary. But its account leaves out the other external news link and the report's emphasis on how recently the interview preceded the announcement. Those details do not prove a financial offer; they do explain why a viewer following the developing story might click through rather than stop at the report.

Just hours before this news broke yesterday I actually spoke to Warren Buffett, who is Wells Fargo's largest shareholder.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A timely report and links to CNBC content are not evidence of a scam mechanism. The reporter discusses Sloan's departure and Buffett's continued support; the supplied calls to action concern subscribing and reading news. Nothing cited asks viewers to claim a reward, make an investment, or transfer funds.

But he says he stands by his support of Sloan in this entire situation.
Get the latest news: http://www.cnbc.com/

opening.argument: Judge, the news format also serves an audience-acquisition purpose. The title foregrounds Buffett's support for an outgoing CEO, while the description presents the interview and then invites viewers to subscribe for more CNBC material, including exclusive video. The interview need not contain a spoken sales pitch for the surrounding presentation to steer viewers toward participation. The question is whether the reporting is doing double duty as promotion for the subscription destination.
